f.title: Cover all areas listed in DIR and REG in risk-based audits of the pharmacovigilance system
f.statement: Risk-based audits of the pharmacovigilance system should cover all areas listed in Directive 2001/83/EC and Regulation (EC) No 726/2004.
f.clause: IV.A. Introduction
f.processes: Audit & inspection readiness; Quality system & CAPA

rows.actor: Organisation (marketing authorisation holder, competent authority in a Member State or the Agency)
rows.quote: Risk-based audits of the pharmacovigilance system should cover all areas listed in Directive 2001/83/EC (DIR) and Regulation (EC) 726/2004 (REG).
rows.location: IV.A. Introduction
rows.review_note: Review: legal basis written out as the instruments the sentence names (no article cited); otherwise no change. Intro summary paragraphs (scope of 'audit', IR article mapping, Section IV.B/IV.C outlines) confirmed as non-requirements. Double-check: intro-level "should" sentence quoted in full; level and scope confirmed; scope is broad (all areas of DIR/REG), so not fully actionable on its own.

f.title: Manage threats to auditor objectivity at all levels
f.statement: Threats to objectivity or the appearance of objectivity (auditors' independence) must be managed at the individual auditor, engagement, functional and organisational levels.
f.clause: IV.A.1. Terminology
f.processes: Audit & inspection readiness; Quality system & CAPA

rows.actor: Organisation (marketing authorisation holder, competent authority in a Member State or the Agency)
rows.quote: Auditors' independence: The freedom from conditions that threaten objectivity or the appearance of objectivity. Such threats to objectivity must be managed at the individual auditor, engagement, functional and organisational levels
rows.location: IV.A.1. Terminology
rows.review_note: Review: kept although it sits in IV.A.1 Terminology: the IIA-derived definition uses 'must' and sets the levels at which threats to objectivity are managed; complements 0040/0041. No change. Double-check: row comes from IV.A.1 Terminology: the "must" sits in an IIA definition borrowed by the Module, not in the Module's own normative text (the Module marks legal duties with "shall" and guidance with "should"). Kept as Mandatory to match the literal wording, but an admin should decide whether a definition belongs in the library at all; substance is also covered by 0040-0042 and 0044.

f.title: Verify appropriateness and effectiveness of the pharmacovigilance system through audit
f.statement: Pharmacovigilance audit activities should verify, by examination and evaluation of objective evidence, the appropriateness and effectiveness of the implementation and operation of a pharmacovigilance system, including its quality system for pharmacovigilance activities.
f.clause: IV.B.1. Pharmacovigilance audit and its objective
f.processes: Audit & inspection readiness; Quality system & CAPA

rows.actor: Organisation (marketing authorisation holder, competent authority in a Member State or the Agency)
rows.quote: Pharmacovigilance audit activities should verify, by examination and evaluation of objective evidence, the appropriateness and effectiveness of the implementation and operation of a pharmacovigilance system, including its quality system for pharmacovigilance activities.
rows.location: IV.B.1. Pharmacovigilance audit and its objective
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: quote proves statement; level, actor and classification confirmed.

f.title: Do not regard activities without independent evidence as audits
f.statement: Benchmarking, reviews of qualifications, risk assessment questionnaires, surveys or other activities in which evidence of fulfilment of pharmacovigilance requirements is not independently obtained and evaluated would not be regarded as an audit.
f.clause: IV.B.1. Pharmacovigilance audit and its objective (footnote 3)
f.processes: Audit & inspection readiness; Quality system & CAPA

rows.actor: Organisation (marketing authorisation holder, competent authority in a Member State or the Agency)
rows.quote: Benchmarking, reviews of qualifications, risk assessment questionnaires, surveys or other activities in which evidence of fulfilment of pharmacovigilance requirements is not independently obtained and evaluated, would not be regarded as an audit.
rows.location: IV.B.1. Pharmacovigilance audit and its objective (footnote 3)
rows.review_note: Review: kept as a definition that decides whether an activity counts toward the legally required audit (footnote 3, added in Rev 1); Recommended because the text is not stated as binding. No change. Double-check: footnote 3 (the Rev 1 explanatory note) is a scope clarification with no modal ("would not be regarded as an audit"); worth keeping because it decides what counts toward the legally required audit, but Recommended is an interpretation of non-modal wording.

f.statement: In the context of pharmacovigilance, audit criteria should reflect the requirements for the pharmacovigilance system, including its quality system for pharmacovigilance activities, as found in the legislation and guidance.
f.clause: IV.B.1. Pharmacovigilance audit and its objective
f.processes: Audit & inspection readiness; Quality system & CAPA

rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: quote proves statement; level, actor and classification confirmed.

f.title: Have the audit strategy endorsed by upper management
f.statement: Strategic level audit planning results in an audit strategy (long term approach), which should be endorsed by upper management.
f.clause: IV.B.2. The risk-based approach to pharmacovigilance audits
f.processes: Audit & inspection readiness; Safety governance

rows.actor: Organisation (marketing authorisation holder, competent authority in a Member State or the Agency)

f.title: Document risk assessment for strategic, tactical and operational audit planning
f.statement: Risk assessment should be documented appropriately for the strategic, tactical and operational planning of pharmacovigilance audit activity in the organisation.
f.clause: IV.B.2. The risk-based approach to pharmacovigilance audits
f.processes: Audit & inspection readiness; Quality system & CAPA

rows.location: IV.B.2. The risk-based approach to pharmacovigilance audits
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: quote proves statement; level, actor and classification confirmed.

f.title: Cover governance, risk management and internal controls of all parts of the PV system in the audit strategy
f.statement: The audit strategy should cover the governance, risk management and internal controls of all parts of the pharmacovigilance system, including: all pharmacovigilance processes and tasks; the quality system for pharmacovigilance activities; interactions and interfaces with other departments, as appropriate; and pharmacovigilance activities conducted by affiliated organisations or activities delegated to another organisation (e.g. regional reporting centres, MAH affiliates or third parties, such as contract organisations and other vendors).
f.clause: IV.B.2.1. Strategic level audit planning
f.processes: Audit & inspection readiness; Partner & vendor oversight; Quality system & CAPA

rows.actor: Organisation (marketing authorisation holder, competent authority in a Member State or the Agency)
rows.quote: The audit strategy should cover the governance, risk management and internal controls of all parts of the pharmacovigilance system including: • all pharmacovigilance processes and tasks; • the quality system for pharmacovigilance activities; • interactions and interfaces with other departments, as appropriate; • pharmacovigilance activities conducted by affiliated organisations or activities delegated to another organisation (e.g. regional reporting centres, MAH affiliates or third parties, such as contract organisations and other vendors).
rows.location: IV.B.2.1. Strategic level audit planning
rows.review_note: Review: no change. The descriptive audit strategy text (high level statement, usually 2-5 years, list of audits that could reasonably be performed) has no modal and is not captured separately. Double-check: quote proves statement; level, actor and classification confirmed. Bullet list fully quoted and reproduced.

f.title: Consider listed risk factors in the audit risk assessment
f.statement: For the purposes of the audit risk assessment, the organisation may consider the risk factors in the non-prioritised, non-exhaustive list of examples given in the Module, including: changes to legislation and guidance; major re-organisation or other re-structuring of the pharmacovigilance system, mergers and acquisitions (for marketing authorisation holders this may significantly increase the number of products covered by the system); change in key managerial function(s); risk to the availability of adequately trained and experienced pharmacovigilance staff (e.g. significant staff turn-over, deficiencies in training processes, re-organisation, increased work volumes); and significant changes to the system since a previous audit (e.g. a new or significantly upgraded pharmacovigilance database, or process changes to address new or amended regulatory requirements).
f.clause: IV.B.2.1. Strategic level audit planning
f.processes: Audit & inspection readiness; Quality system & CAPA

rows.actor: Organisation (marketing authorisation holder, competent authority in a Member State or the Agency)
rows.quote: This is a non-prioritised, non-exhaustive list of examples of risk factors that could be considered for the purposes of a risk assessment: • changes to legislation and guidance; • major re-organisation or other re-structuring of the pharmacovigilance system, mergers, acquisitions (specifically for marketing authorisation holders, this may lead to a significant increase in the number of products for which the system is used); • change in key managerial function(s); • risk to availability of adequately trained and experienced pharmacovigilance staff, e.g. due to significant turn-over of staff, deficiencies in training processes, re-organisation, increase in volumes of work; • significant changes to the system since the time of a previous audit, e.g. introduction of a new database(s) for pharmacovigilance activities or of a significant upgrade to the existing database(s), changes to processes and activities in order to address new or amended regulatory requirements;
rows.location: IV.B.2.1. Strategic level audit planning
rows.review_note: Review: added. The extractor skipped the risk-factor list as examples; as an SME it is the content inspectors check an audit risk assessment against, so it is captured as a Permitted row ('could be considered'). Quote limited to the first five factors (1000-character limit); the remaining factors (first product on the market, products with additional risk minimisation or monitoring, criticality of the process, outcome of previous audits, procedural gaps, compliance information, other organisational changes) follow in IV.B.2.1 and the MAH-specific sentence is row 0009. Double-check: quote and statement cover only the first five of the twelve example risk factors (1000-character quote limit); the remaining factors (first product on the market, products with additional risk minimisation or additional monitoring, criticality of the process, outcome of previous audits, procedural gaps, compliance information, other organisational changes) are not captured except the MAH affiliate sentence in 0009. The list is explicitly non-prioritised, non-exhaustive examples ("could be considered"), so Permitted is a reasonable reading, but whether it is a requirement at all is debatable. Admin to decide whether to add a second row for the rest of the list.

f.statement: When deciding when to audit an affiliate or third party, the marketing authorisation holder should consider the nature and criticality of the pharmacovigilance activities being performed by the affiliate or third party on its behalf, in addition to considering the other risk factors listed.
f.clause: IV.B.2.1. Strategic level audit planning
f.applicability: Affiliates and third parties performing pharmacovigilance activities on behalf of the marketing authorisation holder
f.processes: Audit & inspection readiness; Partner & vendor oversight

rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: quote proves statement; level, actor and classification confirmed.

f.title: Prepare the audit programme in line with the audit strategy
f.statement: An audit programme is a set of one or more audits planned for a specific timeframe, normally for a year. It should be prepared in line with the long term audit strategy.

f.processes: Audit & inspection readiness; Quality system & CAPA

f.title: Base the audit programme on risk assessment and focus it on key areas
f.statement: The risk-based audit programme should be based on an appropriate risk assessment and should focus on: the quality system for pharmacovigilance activities; critical pharmacovigilance processes (see e.g. GVP Module I and IR Art 11, 15); key control systems relied on for pharmacovigilance activities; and areas identified as high risk, after controls have been put in place or mitigating action taken.
f.clause: IV.B.2.2. Tactical level audit planning
f.processes: Audit & inspection readiness; Quality system & CAPA

rows.actor: Organisation (marketing authorisation holder, competent authority in a Member State or the Agency)

f.title: Perform risk-based audits at regular intervals in line with legislation

Kept Mandatory; admin to confirm level.

f.statement: Documents and information collected by the internal auditor should be treated with appropriate confidentiality and discretion, and should also respect Directive 95/46/EC (Regulation (EC) No 45/2001 for Community institutions and bodies) and national legislation on the protection of individuals with regard to the processing of personal data and on the free movement of such data.

A reader acting on the row today must apply the successor laws; admin should decide whether to add a note before publishing.
